question: Do publicly indexed SPCP collection records and WPU-linked Lake Manguao survey material provide a verifiable voucher crosswalk for the historical fish leads?

sourcesReviewed.citation: Froese, R. and D. Pauly (eds.). FishBase, version 06/2026. Occurrence records cite Anonymous (2004), Fish Collection of the Ichthyology Laboratory, State Polytechnic College of Palawan.
sourcesReviewed.access: Reviewed FishBase museum summary, its cited Anonymous (2004) bibliography record, two species occurrence lists, and six individual specimen-detail pages. The legacy museum summary identifies SPCP as State Polytechnic College of Palawan and was last modified in 2011; the occurrence pages were last modified in 2017. These are portal transcriptions, not direct confirmation from the current collection custodian.

catalogRecords.currentNameCrosswalk: Barbodes manguaoensis; FishBase portal's bantolanensis label is a historical/name-status mismatch, not a specimen re-identification.

The 2025 Philippine type checklist crosswalks historical Penesilurus palavanensis/Hito taytayensis usage to Pterocryptis taytayensis; this portal/catalog name mapping is not an independent specimen identification.

reportedScope.underlyingReference: FishBase cites Anonymous (2004), Fish Collection of the Ichthyology Laboratory, State Polytechnic College of Palawan. The FishBase reference entry provides no DOI, PDF, reference URL or item-level reuse terms.
reportedScope.interpretation: Six individually numbered legacy SPCP records are publicly indexed under Lake Manguao and dated 2002. They are historical collection leads; the index does not show exact capture coordinates or station identifiers, and its catalog data could not be checked against the physical specimens or an updated SPCP/WPU catalog.

limits: The SPCP museum summary is a legacy FishBase page last modified in 2011 and does not establish current custody, institutional continuity, or a contactable public catalog.

The underlying Anonymous (2004) collection catalog is identified bibliographically in FishBase but was not found as a separately accessible source; individual FishBase records were last modified in 2017.

FishBase currently states that its content is CC BY-NC 4.0 and requests attribution/linking, but this does not independently settle rights in the underlying 2004 collection catalog or any specimen images. No Bangwit publication approval was made.
No coordinates or station crosswalk are supplied in these six detail pages. Preserve the locality strings; do not manufacture points from a lake centroid or gear notation.

The 2025 WPU-linked project report is a different 2011 survey, not a validation of these 2002 catalog numbers. Its fish table provides site-class labels but no specimen accession codes tying the survey catches to the SPCP records.
The portal's current-name display and taxonomy crosswalk do not re-identify specimens. The Barbodes bantolanensis / B. manguaoensis synonymy must not inflate the accepted-species count.

sourcesReviewed.citation: Anonymous. (2004). Fish Collection of the Ichthyology Laboratory, State Polytechnic College of Palawan. State Polytechnic College of Palawan. FishBase reference no. 50669.
sourcesReviewed.access: Bibliographic metadata only, accessed through FishBase's reference record. No catalog document, dataset file, author list, URL, DOI, license or rights statement was found.

reportedScope.relationship: FishBase cites this collection catalog as the main reference for the six SPCP-numbered Lake Manguao portal entries reviewed in this batch.
reportedScope.interpretation: The citation describes a collection inventory, but it is not itself accessible evidence for each transcribed row beyond the FishBase occurrence pages.

limits: The original catalog was not independently retrieved, so completeness, accession-level wording, identification history and current specimen custody remain unverified.
No rights or public-app reuse terms were verified for the catalog.
Do not treat the cited collection catalog as a fully reviewed or complete Lake Manguao checklist.

sourcesReviewed.citation: Matillano, J. D. and Atrero, L. O. (2013). Conserving Endemic and Globally Threatened Fishes in Lake Manguao, Palawan, Philippines. Conservation Leadership Programme project 0347311 final report; field project September 2011–August 2012.
sourcesReviewed.access: Full 34-page report retrieved from the Conservation Leadership Programme public site and reviewed, including methods, fish-by-station table, sampling-site appendix and diet results. The report identifies Western Philippines University and the Municipality of Taytay as implementation partners. No item-specific reuse license was found.

reportedScope.surveyDesign: The fish table labels nine littoral stations (L1-L9), two open-water stations (O1-O2) and stream station S1, and reports 12 taxa with station/habitat occurrence marks. Methods state sampling in October and December 2011, but the Table 3 caption states October and December 2013, outside the report's September 2011-August 2012 project dates; this conflict is unresolved. The methods prose also says two stream sites were sampled while the table/figure labels only S1. The report provides substrate descriptions and plates but not GPS coordinates or SPCP accession identifiers.
reportedScope.catalogCrosscheck: Names in the report's historical source usage overlap with the SPCP portal's taxon leads, but the report does not link its 2011 specimens to SPCP 0737/0738/0742/0743/0756/0757 or the 2002 catalog.

limits: The WPU-linked report concerns a separate study from the 2002 FishBase/SPCP catalog, but its field-date statements conflict internally (methods: October/December 2011; Table 3 caption: October/December 2013) and its stream-site count is also inconsistent. Do not select a date or station count without clarification.
The report is historical and its collection/station labels do not establish current fish presence, abundance, waterbody-wide absence, catchability or legal access.
It includes a separate Nile tilapia gut-content study; detailed diet extraction and season/size interpretation are deferred to a dedicated diet-source review.
No report-specific data or content reuse license was verified. No table, figure, map, diet values or full species table was copied into the application.

crossSourceAssessment.collectionCatalog: FishBase publicly exposes six records attributed to SPCP and an inaccessible 2004 collection-catalog reference. This is a useful accession-level discovery lead, but not direct museum confirmation. WPU-linked public reporting found in this review does not provide an accession crosswalk or accessible digitized catalog.
crossSourceAssessment.surveySeparation: The 2002 specimen-catalog entries and the WPU-linked survey described in the 2013 report are separate evidence sources. The report's methods say October/December 2011 but Table 3 says 2013, and its stream-site count conflicts; do not state an exact separation interval. It reports 12 taxa from littoral/open-water/stream station classes; no overlap between survey and catalog identifiers is established.
crossSourceAssessment.taxonomicCrosswalk: The FishBase row SPCP 0743 is presented under Barbodes bantolanensis while its source name is Puntius bantolanensis; the current Catalog of Fishes treats the bantolanensis name as a synonym of valid Barbodes manguaoensis. SPCP 0742 separately records the source name Puntius manguaoensis. Keep both catalog accessions as source records, but do not count them as two accepted species. SPCP 0757 uses Hito taytayensis; the 2025 checklist provides a historical-name crosswalk to Pterocryptis taytayensis, not re-identification of the specimen.
crossSourceAssessment.appReadiness: Research-only. The data are historical portal transcriptions with no direct custodian confirmation, exact stations/coordinates, or resolved underlying-catalog rights. The date-conflicted report supplies survey-level context but not voucher codes or public reuse permission. No current presence, absence, abundance, diet, catchability, fishing rules, safety or geometry is approved.

rightsReview.status: FishBase's current general site license is CC BY-NC 4.0; attribution/linking to the portal and original record references is required. Rights in the underlying Anonymous (2004) collection catalog and CLP report were not independently established. The license is not treated as blanket approval for Bangwit public release.
rightsReview.handling: No source files, raw download, specimen image, report table, map, or figure were retained. This JSON stores a limited research crosswalk of six portal records and source limitations.

disposition.reason: The six SPCP-numbered entries are useful historical portal records but the cited source catalog is not independently available, current collection custody and taxon identifications are unverified, and item-level reuse rights and coordinates/stations are unresolved. The separate 2011 WPU-linked survey has no voucher-code crosswalk.

nextAction: Review the 2013 Lake Manguao report's standardized Oreochromis niloticus gut-content results as a separate, lake-and-study-specific diet evidence batch. Preserve the internal field-date and stream-site conflicts plus sample season and size context, distinguish natural diet from bait suggestions, and keep app reuse approval pending; then continue the Luzon freshwater waterbody sequence.
